name: Non-Aligned Movement
title: The story of the Non-Aligned Movement

text: In the Cold War, two great powers formed two sides and tried to pull other countries onto them.
About 70 years ago, leaders of Asian and African countries met at Bandung and promised not to take either side.
src: when two great powers formed blocs / set out to pull the rest of the world into their orbits
The Bandung Conference of Asian and African states, hosted by Indonesia’s president Sukarno in 1955, adopted a declaration that included them and a collective pledge to stay neutral in the Cold War

text: Jawaharlal Nehru of India wanted newly free countries to keep their independence and not be pushed onto one side.
Its members have often disagreed, and some, such as India and Pakistan, have fought each other.
src: it grew from the wish of Jawaharlal Nehru and other leaders of newly independent countries to guard their independence and sovereignty against demands for allegiance to one of two warring superpowers
Members also fought one another, India and Pakistan, Iran and Iraq / members of very different ideologies

text: More than 60 years ago, Tito of Yugoslavia and leaders of Egypt, India, Ghana and Indonesia founded it in Belgrade.
It looks for a middle way between the two great sides.
src: Founded in Belgrade in 1961 on the initiative of Tito, Nasser, Nehru, Nkrumah and Sukarno / Its founders Josip Broz Tito of Yugoslavia, Gamal Abdel Nasser of Egypt, Jawaharlal Nehru of India, Kwame Nkrumah of Ghana and Sukarno of Indonesia
it sought a middle course between the Western and Eastern blocs

text: It campaigned against colonial rule, racism and apartheid, a system of racial discrimination in South Africa.
Today its 120 member countries hold more than half of all the people in the world.
src: campaigned against colonialism, racism and apartheid / South Africa’s apartheid as a form of racial discrimination
its 120 members holding 55% of the world’s population
